headline: Fuel, Peso and Power Pressures Converge as Filipino Households Face a Cost Squeeze
seoTitle: Fuel, Peso and Power Pressures Hit Filipino Households | FMB News
seoDescription: Fuel prices jumped, the peso traded near record lows and the Visayas grid returned to red alert on September 15, while a BIR ruling removed VAT from allowable system-loss charges.
deck: Large fuel-price increases, a peso trading near record lows and another Visayas grid red alert converged on September 15, while a new BIR ruling removed VAT from allowable electricity system-loss charges.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Filipino households faced several cost pressures at once on September 15 as large fuel-price increases took effect, the peso traded close to 63 to the US dollar and the Visayas power grid returned to red alert.
The Department of Energy announced increases of P5.68 per liter for gasoline, P4.31 for diesel and P4.62 for kerosene for the September 15 to 21 pricing week.
The peso touched a fresh intraday low of P62.925 to the dollar before closing at P62.835, 2.5 centavos stronger than the previous session’s record-low close of P62.86.
The Visayas grid was again placed under red alert as available generation remained tight because of plant outages and limited ability to import additional power from Mindanao.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: A weaker peso increases the local-currency cost of dollar-priced imports. That is especially important for the Philippines because the country imports much of the oil it consumes.
Fuel-price increases affect more than motorists. They can raise transport and logistics costs, which can eventually move through supply chains into the prices paid by households and businesses.

There was one measure of relief on electricity bills. The Bureau of Internal Revenue issued Revenue Memorandum Circular 97-2026, recognizing the allowable system-loss charge within the Energy Regulatory Commission cap as a government-mandated charge excluded from gross sales for value-added-tax purposes.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Oil prices, the exchange rate and electricity supply can reinforce one another. Higher global oil prices increase the import bill; a weaker peso makes those imports more expensive; and tight power supply can push electricity-market costs higher.
The VAT treatment of allowable system loss trims one component of electricity bills, but it does not erase the wider pressures from fuel, generation costs or currency weakness.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch global oil prices, any government decision on fuel excise taxes, the peso-dollar rate and whether the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas acts to smooth disorderly currency volatility.
For electricity, watch Visayas generation availability, plant return-to-service schedules and the actual bill impact of the BIR system-loss VAT clarification.
